facts.fact: About 40 percent of US cow-calf operations reported rotational grazing in 2018: 54 percent of retained stocker operations, 50 percent of retained finishers and 38 percent of strict cow-calf producers.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Charts of Note: About 40 percent of all cow-calf operations reported using rotational grazing in 2018 (2022)
facts.quote: About 40 percent of all cow-calf operations reported using a rotational grazing system ... 54 percent of retained stocker operations have adopted some form of rotational grazing. This adoption rate is more than the rate for strictly cow-calf producers, who sell all calves at or around weaning (38 percent), or retained finisher producers, who retain calves until market weight (50 percent).
facts.note: 2018 is the year the source page reports for this figure (from its title, date or text), not a count in the quote.

facts.fact: Before 2022, fewer than 5 percent of US egg-laying hens were raised in states with confinement restrictions in effect. ERS expected that to pass 13 percent by 2026.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Charts of Note: Number of States with restrictions on egg-laying hen confinement is small but growing (2023)
facts.quote: Before 2022, fewer than 5 percent of egg-laying hens were raised in States with implemented restrictions on confined or caged production, but that number is expected to surpass 13 percent by 2026.

facts.fact: Food retail concentration in 2019, on a 0 to 10,000 index, was 593 nationally, 1,332 by state, 1,881 by metro area and 3,737 by county. The smaller the market area, the higher the concentration.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Charts of Note: Food retail concentration increases as geographic area shrinks (2023)
facts.quote: HHI values range from 0 to 10,000 ... As the geographic market area shrinks, the market concentration in 2019 increased from 593 (national) to 1,332 (State) to 1,881 (MSA) to 3,737 (county).

facts.fact: In fiscal 2022 the US imported nearly $3.3 billion of cut flowers, plants and nursery stock from 81 countries. Colombia supplied the most, $1.2 billion.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Charts of Note: U.S. imports of cut flowers and nursery products grew to $3.3 billion in 2022 (2023)
facts.quote: In fiscal year 2022, the United States imported nearly $3.3 billion worth of cut flowers, plants, and nursery stock products from 81 countries. ... Colombia made up the largest import value at $1.2 billion.

facts.fact: ERS estimated 39,534 farm estates were created in 2022. Of those, 305 would have to file an estate tax return and 87 would likely owe estate tax.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Charts of Note: Less than 1 percent of farm estates created in 2022 must file an estate tax return (2023)
facts.quote: Researchers from USDA, Economic Research Service (ERS) estimate that in 2022, 39,534 estates were created from principal operator deaths. Of those estates, ERS forecasts that 305 (0.77 percent) will be required to file an estate tax return, and a further 87 (0.22 percent) will likely owe Federal estate tax.

facts.fact: In 2018, foods labeled "natural" were slightly more than 16 percent of US retail food purchases: 27.7 percent of dairy spending but only 5.4 percent of vegetables.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Charts of Note: Foods with “natural” labels accounted for 16 percent of U.S. consumer food spending in 2018 (2023)
facts.quote: In 2018, food products labeled “natural” accounted for slightly more than 16 percent of all consumer retail food purchases. ... The share of spending on “natural” products in 2018 was highest for dairy products (27.7 percent) and lowest for fruits (5.9 percent) and vegetables (5.4 percent).

facts.fact: US soybean planted acreage grew 18 percent, from 74 million acres in 2002 to 87 million in 2022. Corn grew 12 percent, and wheat fell 22 percent.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Charts of Note: Since early 2000s, growth in U.S. soybean planted acreage has outpaced corn and wheat (2023)
facts.quote: Soybean planted acreage grew by 18 percent, from 74 million in 2002 to 87 million in 2022, while corn planted acreage increased by 12 percent in the same period. In contrast to this growth, wheat planted acres declined 22 percent over the same 20-year period

facts.fact: China's rice stocks for 2018/19 were projected at a record 113 million tons, about 70 percent of the world's. The US was projected to hold 1.5 million tons.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Charts of Note: China holds nearly 70 percent of global rice stocks in storage (2018)
facts.quote: Rice stocks in China continue to climb, with 2018/19 marketing year ending stocks (unused rice kept in storage) projected at a record 113 million tons, or about 70 percent of the world’s stocks. By comparison, the United States is projected to hold 1.5 million tons of rice stocks.

facts.fact: In 2018 Brazil was the world's largest beef exporter, with close to 20 percent of global exports, 527,000 metric tons ahead of second-place India.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Charts of Note: ICYMI... Brazil projected to outpace other top beef-exporting countries over the next decade (2019)
facts.quote: In 2018, Brazil was the world’s largest exporter of beef, providing close to 20 percent of total global beef exports, outpacing India, the second-largest exporter, by 527,000 metric tons carcass weight equivalent (CWE).

facts.fact: Exports were about 10 percent of the 5.7 billion pounds of turkey produced in the US in 2020. China banned US poultry in January 2015 and lifted the ban in November 2019.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Charts of Note: U.S. exports of turkey to China resume in 2020 after trade ban lifted (2021)
facts.quote: Exports accounted for about 10 percent of the 5.7 billion pounds of turkey produced in the United States in 2020. ... In January 2015, China banned all imports of poultry from the United States because of U.S. outbreaks of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI). After nearly 5 years, China lifted its ban on U.S. poultry in November 2019.

facts.fact: In 2018, 72 percent of US counties had at least one farmers market, and 70 percent of those counties had at least one that accepted credit cards.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Charts of Note: More than half of U.S. counties had at least one farmers market that accepted credit cards in 2018 (2022)
facts.quote: In 2018, 72 percent of U.S. counties reported having at least one farmers market, and 70 percent of those counties reported having one or more farmers markets with the option to purchase using credit cards.

facts.fact: Only 48.1 percent of beginning farmers with sales in 2007 also reported sales in 2012, against 55.7 percent of all farms. Those selling direct to consumers survived at 54.3 percent.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Charts of Note: Beginning farms that sell directly to consumers more likely to survive (2016)
facts.quote: only 48.1 percent of beginning farmers with positive sales in 2007 also reported positive sales in 2012—compared with 55.7 percent of all farms. ... As a whole, beginning farms with direct-to-consumer (DTC) sales had a 54.3 percent survival rate

facts.fact: In 2012 the US had 125,441 midsize farms, over 70,000 of them in cash grains and oilseeds. As many as 15 percent of midsize farms will become large farms.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Charts of Note: Midsize farms are more common in the northern Great Plains and Heartland regions (2016)
facts.quote: as many as 15 percent of today’s midsize farms will become tomorrow’s large farms. In 2012, the U.S. had 125,441 midsize farms—the majority of which (over 70,000 farms) specialized in cash grains and oilseed crops.

facts.fact: In 2023, Mexico supplied 63 percent of US vegetable imports and 47 percent of US fruit and nut imports.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Amber Waves: Growth in Mexico’s Horticultural Exports to the United States Continued Even as New U.S. Food Safety Laws Took Effect (2024)
facts.quote: In 2023, Mexico supplied 63 percent of U.S. vegetable imports and 47 percent of U.S. fruit and nut imports.

facts.fact: The US eradicated contagious bovine pleuropneumonia in 1892, foot-and-mouth disease in 1929, screwworms in 1959 and hog cholera in 1978.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Amber Waves: ERS and Collaborators Model Foot-and-Mouth Disease Outbreaks (2008)
facts.quote: Despite some successes in eradicating livestock diseases (contagious bovine pleuropneumonia, 1892; foot-and-mouth disease (FMD), 1929; screwworms, 1959; hog cholera, 1978)

facts.fact: In 2010 about 35 cents of each dollar spent on US-produced food at retail stores went to processors like flour mills, meatpacking plants and dairy processors, up from about 31 cents in 2007.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Amber Waves: Food Processing Costs Per Food-at-Home Dollar Rose Sharply in 2009 and 2010 (2012)
facts.quote: In 2010, about 35 cents from each dollar that U.S. consumers spent on U.S.-produced food sold in grocery and other retail foodstores went to food processing establishments like flour mills, meatpacking plants, and dairy processors. ... when the share was about 31 cents per dollar spent.
facts.note: 2007 is the year the source page reports for this figure (from its title, date or text), not a count in the quote.

facts.fact: ERS's 2014 farm income forecast included $4.4 billion in Livestock Forage Disaster Program payments, an over 700 percent increase over the previous 5 years combined.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Amber Waves: Livestock Forage Disaster Program Payments Increase in 2014 (2015)
facts.quote: ERS’s current farm income forecast for 2014 includes $4.4 billion in Livestock Forage Disaster Program (LFP) payments, an over 700-percent increase from total LFP payments made during the previous 5 years combined.

facts.fact: In 2005 ERS estimated greenhouse tomatoes were 17 percent of the US fresh tomato supply, and 37 percent of fresh tomatoes sold in US retail stores, against negligible amounts in the early 1990s.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Amber Waves: North American Greenhouse Tomatoes Emerge as a Major Market Force (2005)
facts.quote: Greenhouse tomatoes now represent an estimated 17 percent of U.S. fresh tomato supply. ... Around 37 percent of all fresh tomatoes sold in U.S. retail stores are now greenhouse, compared with negligible amounts in the early 1990s.
facts.note: 2005 is the year the source page reports for this figure (from its title, date or text), not a count in the quote.

facts.fact: At its peak, the Gulf of Mexico dead zone covers about 7,000 square miles, an area as large as New Jersey. Scientists believe nitrogen loads from the Mississippi River cause it.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Amber Waves: Dead Zone in the Gulf: Addressing Agriculture's Contribution (2003)
facts.quote: covering about 7,000 square miles, an area as large as New Jersey. ... Scientists believe that Gulf hypoxia is caused by nitrogen loads from the Mississippi River.

facts.fact: In 2013 the US exported organic products to over 80 countries and imported them from nearly 100. Tracked organic exports were $537 million and imports $1.4 billion.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Amber Waves: U.S. Organic Trade Includes Fresh Produce Exports and Tropical Imports (2014)
facts.quote: In 2013, the United States exported organic products consisting mostly of fresh fruits and vegetables to over 80 countries and imported organic products, including coffee, bananas, and olive oil, from nearly 100 countries. ... In 2013, the value of tracked U.S. organic exports was $537 million, and the value of tracked U.S. organic imports was $1.4 billion.

facts.fact: In strip-till for row crops, seeds are planted into narrow strips, typically 6-8 inches, that were tilled. No-till plants straight into the previous crop's residue.
facts.source: USDA Economic Research Service, Amber Waves: No-Till or Strip-Till Use Varies by Region (2016)
facts.quote: In a no-till system, farmers plant directly into the undisturbed residue of the previous crop without tillage, except for nutrient injection. In a strip-till system for row crops, seeds are planted into narrow strips (typically 6-8 inches) that were tilled and where fertilizer may also be applied.
